edit.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: documented real-product background-edit test for a public comparison page
Primary request: Replace only the surrounding environment with a clean, pale neutral-gray studio tabletop and seamless neutral-gray studio background. Remove the drinking glass, paper/map, wooden table, and distant background objects.
Input image: the provided photograph is the edit target.
Subject invariants: Preserve the red 330 mL Coca-Cola can exactly as shown, including its position, crop, proportions, silhouette, opened top, highlights, red color, every visible printed word and logo, the 330 mL marking, and the tiny yellow-and-black football referee figurine sitting on the can. Preserve the subject's original viewing angle and scale.
Composition/framing: keep the original landscape framing and the can in the same location; do not zoom or crop the can.
Lighting: neutral soft studio light while retaining physically plausible reflections on the unchanged can.
Constraints: one actual output only; change only background and surrounding non-product objects; no added text, no added products, no watermark, no redesign, no repaired or invented package text.
Avoid: altering the can, label, logo, typography, printed claims, color, tab/opening, or figurine.

humanObservation.background: The glass, paper, wooden table, and distant objects were replaced by a neutral studio setting.
humanObservation.retained: The red can, opened top, referee figurine, visible Coca-Cola mark, ORIGINAL TASTE line, Las Vegas promotion and 330 mL marking remain recognizable in the only output.
humanObservation.changedOrUncertain: The can's full-frame position and relative size appear similar at the displayed scale; no precise pixel-alignment measurement was completed. Lighting, highlights, and some surface rendering changed. Character-level identity cannot be proven by unaided visual inspection alone.
humanObservation.comparisonWithMachine: The human observation agrees that the five reported identity/component attributes appear preserved at the displayed scale. The human separately records rerendered lighting and surface detail; Pairvu routed the case to REVIEW because full packaging shape/proportions were not sufficiently comparable.

claimBoundary: One licensed-photo edit and one Pairvu run support only this case report. They do not establish population accuracy, brand endorsement, current packaging, customer demand, or a quality benchmark.
